newsitem.title: UK: Stagecoach slide continues, boss buys shares.
newsitem.headline: Stagecoach slide continues, boss buys shares.

text.p: Stagecoach Plc's executive chairman Brian Souter scooped up another 10,000 shares in the company on behalf of his wife on Monday as other investors continued to bale out.

Shares in the British transport group which owns South West Trains -- a privatised operator facing threats of a one million stg fine or loss of its licence after missing performance targets -- saw its value slump another 36 1/2 pence to 642 1/2.
The latest trigger for the share price slide was a negative report in the Financial Times' Lex column which put a valuation of 540 pence on the shares.EF
The FT said the valuation was based on what it described as "far from gloomy" assumptions about its bus operations, its SW Trains unit and the Porterbrook rolling stock leasing company.

Stagecoach shares had already fallen by 52 pence on Wednesday and Thursday last week amid fears of a regulatory clampdown under a possible Labour government. The election is on May 1, with Labour riding high in opinion polls.
But despite this gloomy background, Brian Souter, the executive chairman of Stagecoach, bought another 10,000 shares for his wife Elizabeth.
The ordinary shares were bought at 645 pence per share, taking their combined holding to 36,524,090 shares.
